note: Trainable: eligible for the fine-tune query distribution. Probes anchored in the Phaedrus' own myths (the chariot, the invention of letters, the regrowth of wings) to separate it from the other four Platonic dialogues.

queries.query: the soul pictured as a charioteer driving a pair of winged horses, one noble and responsive, the other unruly and dragging the team down toward earth
queries.note: The chariot image; the bad horse's description ('crooked lumbering animal', 'short thick neck', 'shag-eared and deaf, hardly yielding to whip and spur') paraphrased away; 'charioteer' kept — the image is known by that name.

queries.query: why Socrates, retelling an old Egyptian story about the inventor of letters, says that writing weakens memory and gives readers only an appearance of knowing without real understanding
queries.note: The critique of writing; 'aid not to memory, but to reminiscence', 'semblance of truth', 'show of wisdom without the reality', 'garden of letters' paraphrased away.

queries.query: why the lover trembles with reverence at the sight of a beautiful face: earthly beauty stirs the memory of what his soul once beheld beyond the heavens, and the soul's wings begin to sprout again
queries.note: Recollection of true beauty and the regrowth of wings; 'a shudder runs through him', 'the old awe steals over him', 'transported with the recollection', 'bird fluttering and looking upward' paraphrased away.

queries.query: can madness be a gift from the gods — prophetic inspiration that comes only when someone is out of their ordinary mind
queries.note: Divine madness and the Delphic prophetess; ecstatic inspiration as sacred rather than sick is answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: should the deepest teachings be written down, or passed on living from teacher to student
queries.note: Writing as recreation versus the living word planted in a soul; oral transmission of doctrine is a pan-traditional concern. No target — graded post-hoc.
